title: Pahang Sultanate
capsule: The Pahang Sultanate is one of the oldest Malay Muslim polities on the eastern Malay Peninsula, with roots in the fifteenth century as a vassal of the Malacca Sultanate; the modern dynasty traces its foundation to Ahmad ibn Tun Ali, who was installed as sultan in 1882 following a succession dispute that drew Siamese and British intervention. Britain formalized its protectorate relationship through the Pahang Treaty of 1887 and incorporated Pahang into the Federated Malay States in 1895. Pahang became part of independent Malaya in 1957, and the current ruler of Malaysia (Yang di-Pertuan Agong since 2019) is Sultan Abdullah of Pahang.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Pahang's territorial extent as a nineteenth-century sultanate is documented in British colonial records; earlier boundary definitions are imprecise.
